advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Document (or narrow) the parity contract: compare_parity only detects (target,direction,action) triple-set differences, not payload or multiplicity divergences.
evidence: compare_parity builds `shadow_set = {(m.target, m.direction.value, m.action.value) for plan in ticket_plans for m in plan.mutations}` and diffs `legacy_set - shadow_set` / `shadow_set - legacy_set` — payload and multiplicity are dropped
ParityReport docstring claims `deltas` is 'every observed difference' (ticket_plan.py:130-134), broader than the triple-set comparison actually detects
advisory.finding: compare_parity reduces legacy mutations and shadow-plan mutations to a set of (target, direction, action) triples, so any divergence that is payload-only or a duplicate-triple count difference is invisible and parity reports matched=True — the oracle cannot distinguish 'identical' from 'differs only in a dimension the triple omits'.
scenarios: A shadow plan preserves a mutation's (target,direction,action) but mutates its payload — parity reports matched=True while a real behavioral divergence exists
Legacy emits two mutations with an identical triple but shadow emits one — the count difference collapses in the set and is not flagged

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a narrow-signature applier.apply is NOT handed ticket_plans and a ticket_plans-accepting applier IS, via reconcile's forwarding gate.
evidence: reconcile.py:517-521 adds `_ticket_plans_kw = ({"ticket_plans": getattr(ctx, "ticket_plans", None)} if getattr(ctx, "ticket_plans", None) is not None and _accepts_ticket_plans(applier.apply) else {})`
reconcile_helpers.py:643 adds `def _accepts_ticket_plans(fn)` returning True on a `ticket_plans` param or VAR_KEYWORD
search of the whole repo for `_accepts_ticket_plans` returns only the two src definitions/uses — no test references it

Named violating input: a stub `applier.apply(mutations, ...)` with a fixed signature lacking `ticket_plans` and no **kwargs, driven with a ctx carrying non-None ticket_plans — the gate must suppress the kwarg or apply() raises TypeError
advisory.finding: The new narrow-signature forwarding gate for ticket_plans in reconcile.py (and its helper _accepts_ticket_plans) has no test. No test verifies that a resolved applier.apply whose signature does NOT accept ticket_plans is spared the kwarg (avoiding the TypeError-abort the commit message warns about), nor that an applier that DOES accept it receives ctx.ticket_plans.
scenarios: A future edit inverts the gate condition or _accepts_ticket_plans mis-detects VAR_KEYWORD, silently passing an unexpected kwarg to a narrow stub/applier and aborting the pass
advisory.suggested_fix: Add unit tests calling _accepts_ticket_plans on a fn with/without a ticket_plans param and a **kwargs fn, plus a reconcile-level test with a stub applier of each signature asserting the kwarg is forwarded only when accepted.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test driving applier.apply(..., ticket_plans=plans) that asserts the rendered manifest gains lifecycle_intents.
evidence: applier.py adds `ticket_plans=None` param (line ~372) and forwards `ticket_plans=ticket_plans` to _emit_mode_manifest (line ~529)
The T3 tests call `apply_planning_mod._emit_mode_manifest(...)` directly via `_emit(...)` (test lines ~1013-1035), bypassing applier.apply
ABSENCE: no test invokes applier.apply(..., ticket_plans=...) to assert the passthrough reaches the manifest renderer
advisory.finding: applier.apply()'s new ticket_plans passthrough is not tested at the apply() entry point; only apply_planning._emit_mode_manifest is driven directly. No test confirms apply() forwards ticket_plans into _emit_mode_manifest.
scenarios: apply()'s forwarding line is dropped or renamed while _emit_mode_manifest keeps working; the additive section would silently vanish from the real apply path

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a compare_parity test where a plan's mutations include a triple not in legacy, asserting a delta with kind 'mutation_added'.
evidence: test_compare_parity_reports_identity_version_and_fields and _approved use `_deferred_plans` (defer -> disposition + mutation_dropped); test_compare_parity_matches_on_happy_corpus has empty deltas
ABSENCE: no test constructs a ticket_plan whose mutations contain a triple absent from legacy_mutations, so kind=='mutation_added' is never asserted
advisory.finding: The compare_parity 'mutation_added' branch (shadow_set - legacy_set) is added but never exercised. All parity tests feed the planner mutations derived from the same legacy list, so no fixture produces a shadow-only triple; only the disposition-delta and (incidentally) mutation_dropped paths are hit.
scenarios: A logic error in the shadow_set/legacy_set difference for the added branch would go undetected
